Shared facts and bounded resources support each query

Answer

YASP shares schema facts and application datasets, caches raw results when enabled, and keeps source capacity and transaction affinity under engine control.

  1. Catalog generations describe source structure; application datasets describe application mappings.12
  2. Raw cache replay still applies current application routing and result processing.34
  3. One occupied-capacity budget covers configured adapters and metadata work.5

Lineage follows the effective syntax tree after SQL modification. Selection receives static AST facts before execution. Result hooks receive facts aligned with actual output columns by ordinal; uncertain shapes stay explicit.36

Recognized discovery requests read a fresh catalog generation without acquiring a source session or invoking ordinary query hooks. Expired metadata fails rather than triggering live discovery.71

One configured discovery view

The shared catalog reflects its configured source identity and schema scope. It is not a per-viewer authorization decision or an automatic union of all routed sources. Failed refresh retains the previous complete generation without extending its age. Missing lineage facts remain uncertainty, not permission.

How do application mappings stay shared?

Diagram structure
  • Start or refresh start
  • Claim refresh lease claim
  • Run dataset loader loader
  • Current live dataset live
  • Bound and publish validate

  • Read inside callback lookup

  • claim → loader · Acquired
  • live → lookup
  • loader → validate
  • lookup → context

  • validate → keep · Failed
  • validate → live · Publish

Configured loaders run before serving and can refresh on a schedule. Startup failures prevent service; later refresh failures preserve the last good data.2

Dataset reads are bounded and scoped to the current callback. Each lookup reads the current published value; the registry is separate from the result cache.8

These output rules illustrate configured callbacks. No caller-specific transformation is stored in the raw cache.49

Re-evaluated on a hitReused until expiry
Query context and optional SQL modificationEligible raw source rows

Raw scope includes effective query identity, the selected source/login, frontend identity/database, input dialect, and relevant session/settings. Application values and hook versions are not automatically cache-key fields.1011

The cache changes the access freshness boundary

A hit does not execute source grants or source row policies again until expiry. Route validation and current result hooks still run. Put source-side tenant filtering in effective SQL or the validated route/scope. SQL comment tags alone do not isolate raw cached data. Cache errors and ineligible requests use normal source execution. Explicit transactions bypass the result cache.

Who owns capacity and session continuity?

TriggerRuntime behavior
Selected class has several instancesTry eligible instances within that configured class
No capacity is availableWait under the acquisition deadline or fail
Query finishes but its connection stays pooledPhysical resource capacity can remain occupied
Cleanup or disposal is still runningKeep capacity until resource ownership ends
Valid raw cache hit or metadata snapshot responseAcquire no source execution capacity
Catalog refreshUse normal source admission

Overflow never selects a more privileged login, another target, or another compute class. Submitted SQL and source permission failures are not replayed on another instance.12

Explicit blocks bypass result caching. A conflicting route is rejected; a failed transaction requires rollback before more data queries. Adapter cleanup ends the retained source state.131415
